title: KLC Help
release_note: New Security help area: user/admin roles, user login, views, default passwords, password change, recovery, protected beta update flow and offline language package upload.

sections.title: Quick start
sections.body:
1. Power the controller and open the WebUI.
2. Check the network.
3. Check for firmware and help updates.
4. Set up outputs and pixel counts.
5. Verify LED type, LED count and color order with the edge blink test.
6. Set power limits.
7. Test scenes or sequences.
8. Set up ETS and link KNX/BAOS datapoints.
9. Save a backup.

sections.title: First commissioning
sections.body: For first commissioning, start by testing only a short LED string or a single output. This lets you safely verify data direction, ground connection, level shifter, LED type and color order. Only when this test runs cleanly, enable further outputs and enter the final pixel counts.

sections.title: Safety and power supply
sections.body: LED strips can draw very high currents. Power supply, feed-in points, wire cross-sections and fuses must match the real installation. The power limiter is a software aid and does not replace electrical protection. The ground of controller, level shifter and LED power supply must be connected.

sections.title: Dashboard
sections.body: The dashboard is the overview for normal operation and opens from the KLC logo in the top-left corner. The tile Outputs / scene / estimated load shows every configured output with its status. Disabled outputs are explicitly shown as disabled, count as 0 mA and show Output disabled as scene/test. Warnings on the dashboard mean: open the detail page and read the diagnosis there.

sections.title: Language and view mode
sections.body: The WebUI can be displayed in several languages. The view mode hides or shows expert areas. The normal view is meant for end users; for commissioning, KNX, diagnostics and release work the expert/admin view should be used.

sections.title: Network
sections.body: The network page shows Ethernet and, on the W build, WLAN client and access point separately. Ethernet, WLAN client and AP can exist in parallel depending on the board profile. The WebUI is reachable via all active interfaces; the priority mainly affects outgoing connections such as update and help downloads.

sections.title: Setting up Ethernet
sections.body: Ethernet is the preferred stable connection for installation and updates. DHCP is usually the simplest choice. Use static IP addresses only if gateway, subnet and DNS are known correctly. With a wrong static configuration the controller can become hard to reach on the network.

sections.title: WLAN client and access point
sections.body: The WLAN client connects the controller to an existing WLAN. The access point is meant as a service access. Passwords are not displayed in the WebUI and are not exported in the normal backup. Empty password fields mean: keep the stored password.

sections.title: Fallback IP / emergency access
sections.body: The fallback IP is an emergency access for cases where the normal network configuration is not reachable, for example after DHCP problems or a faulty static configuration. The fallback address must match the maintenance network and must not duplicate a productive address. After repairing the main configuration, check whether the fallback is still needed.

sections.title: Outputs / LED strings
sections.body: This page describes the provided board outputs. The current KLC board provides a hardware maximum of 5 outputs. The summary keeps only the practically relevant counters: active outputs, power groups, global brightness and running manual tests. Disabled outputs stay stored but are not passed to the LED backend.

sections.title: Current output diagnosis
sections.body: The diagnosis shows status, pixels, LED profile, safe current limit, live load, scene/test and active LEDs. A disabled output is deliberately switched off, is shown with 0 mA and also appears as disabled on the dashboard. Manual tests override the normal scene until they are cleared or ended when leaving the page.

sections.title: Testing an LED output
sections.body: For testing, first enable only one output. Keep the pixel count low or work with a short test string. Then run the edge blink test for red, green, blue and, for RGBW, white as well. If colors are swapped, correct the color order. If nothing lights up at all, check ground, data direction, level shifter, GPIO and LED voltage.

sections.title: LED backend and profiles
sections.body: The LED page is an expert view of the technical LED output. It shows whether the LED backend drives real LEDs or works only virtually, and which timing profiles the configured outputs use. If the backend is not ready, configuration values are processed but no LEDs are driven.

sections.title: Power / power limiter
sections.body: The power limiter estimates the LED current and can limit brightness. It works with the controller limit, power groups, string limits, safety factor and current profile. The values are planning and protection values, not a measurement.

sections.title: Power groups / power supplies
sections.body: A power group typically corresponds to one power supply or one shared power domain. Outputs connected to the same power supply should be assigned to the same group. The group limit must be less than or equal to the safely usable power of the supply.

sections.title: Measuring the current profile
sections.body: The measurement function helps to determine realistic mA/pixel values. Procedure: measure with LEDs off, then switch a defined number of LEDs to red, green, blue and optionally white, measure the current and apply the values. This improves the estimate compared to generic default values.

sections.title: Control
sections.body: The control page is meant for direct operation: start a scene, switch off directly or test current values. If KNX sends commands at the same time, the visible state can be influenced by KNX, the WebUI or a manual test.

sections.title: Scenes and sequences
sections.body: Sequences define what a scene does visually. A scene is the storage slot and the KNX/WebUI number; the sequence defines start, main and off behavior. After larger changes, use a preview and then a real output test.

sections.title: Sequence editor
sections.body: The editor loads large sequence data separately to save RAM. Names, copying, resetting and preview are tools for maintaining scenes. Before overwriting a target sequence, check whether it is already used productively via KNX.

sections.title: Preview
sections.body: The preview shows a computed LED frame in the browser. It does not replace a hardware test, but helps checking effect logic, direction, segments, speed and timing.

sections.title: KNX / BAOS
sections.body: KNX/BAOS connects the controller to the KNX system. The firmware works with fixed object numbers and configurable BAOS datapoints. After the initial ETS setup, object numbers should only be changed deliberately and documented.

sections.title: Datapoints and objects
sections.body: Global objects control central functions such as on/off, scene and brightness. Output objects control individual LED outputs. Status objects report state back. A datapoint number of 0 usually means: this object is disabled.

sections.title: Lock and force
sections.body: Lock objects prevent normal operation while the lock is active. Force objects override normal scene commands with a defined action. The active level is important: depending on the setting, value 0 or value 1 activates the function.

sections.title: KNX system diagnostics
sections.body: The KNX system page is for commissioning: test baud rate, query BAOS firmware, read descriptions and values, send status and test loopback. It remains available from the admin area after an administrator signs in. This page is meant for diagnostics and should not be needed in normal operation.

sections.title: Configuration and backup
sections.body: Before updates, larger KNX changes and experiments, always download a backup. An import replaces the stored configuration after validation. Password fields for WLAN/AP are not output as plain text in the normal export.

sections.title: Admin area
sections.body: The admin area is protected by an admin code and is meant for commissioning, diagnostics, JSON endpoints and deep technical information. The code is an operating hurdle, not full network protection; the controller should only be operated in trusted networks.

sections.title: Firmware update
sections.body: The update page checks online versions, downloads firmware or accepts local BIN files. Before updates, preferably save a backup and switch the LED outputs dark. Do not disconnect the power supply during the update.

sections.title: Version history and rollback
sections.body: The version history lists installable firmware versions. This allows an update to a newer version or a deliberate rollback to an earlier state. Save a backup before every rollback, because older firmware may not know newer configuration fields.

sections.title: Updating the help
sections.body: The help can be updated separately from the firmware. The built-in help is always available. With internet access, an authenticated administrator can load the current language file from releases/firmware/klc/help and store it permanently in LittleFS. Reading and searching help remains available to normal users.

sections.title: System diagnostics
sections.body: The system page shows firmware profile, network, memory, LED backend, power limiter, KNX/BAOS, OTA and diagnostics. In case of errors, first open the affected block, then create a support snapshot.

sections.title: Support snapshot
sections.body: The support snapshot collects profile, version, pins, network, OTA, memory and recent events. For support questions, copy this snapshot because it is much more precise than a description from memory.

sections.title: Event list
sections.body: The event list collects errors, warnings and important runtime events. It is often the fastest entry point for sporadic problems. Before clearing, document relevant entries or save a support snapshot, otherwise diagnostic hints are lost.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.body: LEDs stay dark: check output active, pixel count, GPIO, ground, data direction, level shifter, LED voltage and color order. KNX does not respond: check BAOS ready, baud rate, datapoints, object mapping and lock/force. Update does not work: check network, DNS, update path, profile and free storage.

sections.title: LED memory, pending activation and recovery
sections.body: Active means a configuration that completed the entire startup path. Test values on /outputs are volatile RAM values, reuse the fixed test pool and are never saved automatically. Saved structural changes are pending and become active only after a reboot. Pending becomes Last Known Good only after the master pool, ranges, PIO, DMA, every required output and the 64 KiB system reserve have succeeded. A failure is rolled back completely and Last Known Good is started; if that also fails, LEDs remain off in safe recovery mode while WebUI and service AP stay reachable. The LED budget is 128 KiB including the test pool. Zero pixels are allowed only for a volatile no-output test; one pixel safely uses pixel 0 for both ends; up to 800 is normal, 801 to 1200 is the warning range, and 1201 is rejected. A chained output is protected as a complete chain and a follower is never tested alone.

fields.label: Language
fields.short: Selects the language of the WebUI and the help.
fields.details: The help page loads the matching file help_de.json, help_en.json, help_fr.json, help_es.json, help_it.json, help_nl.json or help_pl.json.

fields.label: View
fields.short: Switches between normal and extended operation.
fields.details: Expert areas such as LED, control, KNX and deep diagnostics can be hidden so that normal operation stays clear.

fields.label: Device name
fields.short: Free name for recognizing the controller.
fields.details: The name helps in backups, support snapshots and with several controllers in the same project.

fields.label: Hostname
fields.short: Network name of the controller.
fields.details: Only use characters that resolve cleanly in the local network. After a change, a restart is usually advisable.

fields.label: Ethernet active
fields.short: Switches the W5500 Ethernet interface on or off.
fields.details: Ethernet should stay active if no safe alternative access is set up.

fields.label: DHCP
fields.short: Obtain the IP address automatically from the router.
fields.details: Recommended for most installations. Use static addresses only if the network data is known reliably.

fields.label: Static IP
fields.short: Fixed IP address for the controller.
fields.details: Only effective when DHCP is switched off. Must match the subnet and must not be assigned twice.

fields.label: Gateway
fields.short: Router address for connections to the internet.
fields.details: Without a correct gateway, online updates and help downloads do not work.

fields.label: DNS
fields.short: Name server for internet addresses.
fields.details: Without DNS the controller cannot resolve raw.githubusercontent.com.

fields.label: WLAN SSID
fields.short: Name of the WLAN for client mode.
fields.details: Only available on the W build. Spelling must match the WLAN exactly.

fields.label: WLAN password
fields.short: Password for the WLAN client.
fields.details: An empty field means: keep the stored password. The password is not exported in the standard backup.

fields.label: Access point active
fields.short: Starts a local service access.
fields.details: The AP is practical for maintenance but should be deliberately secured and documented.

fields.label: Outgoing route
fields.short: Priority for outgoing connections.
fields.details: Affects online updates, help downloads and other outgoing HTTP connections. Automatic or Ethernet first is usually sensible.

fields.label: Name
fields.short: Display name of the LED output.
fields.details: Meaningful names like Ceiling, Wall left or Display case make diagnosis, KNX mapping and support easier.

fields.label: Active
fields.short: Switches an LED output on or off logically.
fields.details: Disabled means: values stay stored, but the output is not driven physically and is shown as disabled in the diagnosis.

fields.label: Pixels
fields.short: Number of LEDs on the physical string.
fields.details: The value must match the real LED count. Wrong values lead to cut-off effects, wrong current estimates or a mismatching preview.

fields.label: Equal string segments
fields.short: Splits a physical string into equal repetitions.
fields.details: 1 means a normal string. More segments are helpful when the same effect should repeat on several equally long parts.

fields.label: LED offset
fields.short: Shifts the perceived starting point of the output.
fields.details: Useful for correcting joints, center or running direction. The allowed range is limited so the setting does not accidentally create extreme shifts.

fields.label: After power interruption
fields.short: Defines the behavior after restart or power failure.
fields.details: Off stays dark. Last setting restores the last known state. Fixed scene always starts the selected scene.

fields.label: Fixed scene
fields.short: Scene started after a power interruption.
fields.details: Only relevant when After power interruption is set to Fixed scene.

fields.label: Send LED data
fields.short: Selects physical output only on change or additionally at intervals.
fields.details: Only on change: the LED buffer is transmitted when its content changes. On change and cyclically: additionally the latest valid physical LED buffer is retransmitted at the send interval. Cyclic sending never restarts a scene, animation, random value, ramp or time control, never reinterprets KNX state and never writes to flash.

fields.label: Send interval
fields.short: Time between additional periodic transmissions.
fields.details: Used only in cyclic mode. Allowed values: 1 s, 5 s, 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 10 min, 30 min, 1 h; default 10 s. The interval applies per output. Only the currently valid LED buffer is retransmitted; running animations already transmit on change and automatically postpone the next cyclic transmission.

fields.label: LED chip
fields.short: Timing profile of the installed LED strip.
fields.details: Must match the strip. Wrong timing can lead to flicker, wrong colors or no output at all.

fields.label: LED colors
fields.short: RGB or RGBW per LED.
fields.details: RGBW sends an additional white channel. The value must match the real LED.

fields.label: Color order
fields.short: Corrects swapped color channels.
fields.details: If red, green or blue are displayed wrongly during the test, adjust the order here.

fields.label: Blink start/end
fields.short: Tests the first and last LED of an output.
fields.details: This quickly verifies data direction, string end, color order and physical assignment.

fields.label: Power group
fields.short: Assigns the output to a power supply / power domain.
fields.details: Outputs on the same power supply should use the same power group.

fields.label: String limit mA
fields.short: Maximum allowed current for this output.
fields.details: The power limiter uses this value for warnings and dimming. Choose a value matching the wiring and feed-in.

fields.label: Max. brightness
fields.short: Limits the brightness of an output.
fields.details: 0 stays dark, 255 is full brightness. Lower values reduce all colors of this output.

fields.label: Manual tests active
fields.short: Number of currently running manual color or edge tests.
fields.details: 0 means: no output is currently overridden by a manual test. With active tests, evaluate normal scenes only after the test ends.

fields.label: Global brightness
fields.short: Global brightness limit 0 to 255.
fields.details: Acts as central dimming. 255 is full brightness; 0 makes the output dark.

fields.label: Controller limit mA
fields.short: Total current limit for the controller.
fields.details: Should match the safely usable total power. The value is a software limit, not an electrical fuse.

fields.label: Base current mA
fields.short: Fixed, non-dimmable current share.
fields.details: Typically from a measurement with all LEDs off. Counted in the total limit.

fields.label: Safety %
fields.short: Safety factor for current limits.
fields.details: Reduces usable limits so that reserve remains for measurement inaccuracy, temperature and power supply aging.

fields.label: R/G/B/W mA per pixel
fields.short: Current model for the individual color channels.
fields.details: The more precise these values are, the better the current estimate fits. Ideally determine them with the measurement function.

fields.label: Standby mA/LED
fields.short: Quiescent current per LED.
fields.details: Only use if this share is not already contained in the base current, otherwise it is counted twice.

fields.label: Active power groups
fields.short: Number of power supply groups in use.
fields.details: Only enable as many groups as really needed. The assignment should reflect the real power supply layout so that group limits and warnings are meaningful.

fields.label: Power group limit mA
fields.short: Current limit for one group.
fields.details: Must match the fusing and the power supply of this group.

fields.label: Test output
fields.short: Output for the current profile measurement.
fields.details: Choose an easily accessible output with a known LED count.

fields.label: Measurement LEDs
fields.short: Number of LEDs switched for the measurement.
fields.details: Do not measure more LEDs than the power supply and measurement setup can safely feed.

fields.label: Name
fields.short: Display name of a scene or sequence.
fields.details: Meaningful names make KNX mapping and operation easier.

fields.label: Copy selected sequence to
fields.short: Duplicates a sequence to a target slot.
fields.details: The target sequence is overwritten. Check beforehand whether it is used productively.

fields.label: Reset sequence
fields.short: Resets the selected sequence to factory default.
fields.details: Only reset the selected sequence, then run a preview and a real test.

fields.label: KNX active
fields.short: Enables KNX/BAOS processing.
fields.details: When switched off, KNX commands are ignored and no status values are sent.

fields.label: Baud rate
fields.short: UART speed to the BAOS module.
fields.details: Must match the BAOS module. In case of problems use auto baud or the system diagnostics.

fields.label: Send status
fields.short: Defines when status objects are sent to the bus.
fields.details: Passive sends only manually/on request. Change sends on state changes. Time sends cyclically. Combination uses both.

fields.label: Status interval
fields.short: Time between cyclic status messages.
fields.details: Too short intervals can load the bus unnecessarily. 0 is not meant as a normal cycle value here.

fields.label: BAOS datapoint number
fields.short: Number of the datapoint or object.
fields.details: 0 usually means disabled. After the initial ETS setup, change only deliberately.

fields.label: Central on/off
fields.short: KNX object for the central switching command.
fields.details: Value 0 switches off directly, value 1 starts the on state.

fields.label: Central scene selection
fields.short: Starts a scene via KNX.
fields.details: The received value is mapped to the corresponding scene.

fields.label: Central brightness
fields.short: Brightness value 0 to 255.
fields.details: Can centrally influence the WebUI or scene brightness.

fields.label: Central color R/G/B/W
fields.short: Direct color components 0 to 255.
fields.details: On RGB outputs, white is ignored or processed appropriately, depending on the runtime logic.

fields.label: Output on/off
fields.short: Switch object for a single output.
fields.details: Only affects the assigned output and can be overridden by lock/force.

fields.label: Output scene
fields.short: Scene selection for a single output.
fields.details: Useful when different outputs should be controlled independently.

fields.label: Lock object
fields.short: Locks normal operation of an output.
fields.details: Mind the active level: depending on the setting, value 0 or value 1 locks.

fields.label: Force object
fields.short: Forces a defined action.
fields.details: Force overrides normal scene commands while it is active.

fields.label: Action on lock/force
fields.short: Defines what happens with an active or inactive object.
fields.details: Typical actions are off, on or no change. Test with ETS group addresses before productive use.

fields.label: Beta versions
fields.short: Allows test versions.
fields.details: Enable only deliberately. Beta versions can contain new features but also bugs.

fields.label: Check automatically
fields.short: Checks online for new firmware.
fields.details: Requires a working internet connection, DNS and a matching update path.

fields.label: Install automatically
fields.short: Installs found updates without a further click.
fields.details: Practical, but risky with test versions. Use very deliberately for productive installations.

fields.label: Local BIN file
fields.short: Upload a firmware file from the browser.
fields.details: Only use firmware matching this profile. Download a backup first.

fields.label: Search help
fields.short: Searches titles, pages, short texts and details.
fields.details: Suitable for terms like pixels, KNX, gateway, force, backup, update or manual tests. The search also normalizes German umlauts: Ausgänge and Ausgaenge return the same hits.

fields.label: Update help
fields.short: Loads the current help file for the active language.
fields.details: This permanent LittleFS write requires an administrator login and CSRF protection. Without internet, the built-in help remains available.

fields.label: Download backup
fields.short: Saves the current configuration as JSON.
fields.details: Always create a backup before updates, KNX changes and larger tests.

fields.label: Import backup
fields.short: Loads a stored configuration.
fields.details: The file is validated. Still check beforehand that it matches the firmware profile and the installation.

fields.label: Clear events
fields.short: Empties the event list.
fields.details: Only clear after documentation or a support snapshot, otherwise important diagnostic hints are lost.

fields.label: Fallback IP active
fields.short: Enables a substitute IP if the normal network configuration is not reachable.
fields.details: Helps with DHCP/IP problems. The fallback address must be reachable in the local maintenance network and must not duplicate a productive address.

fields.label: Fallback IP
fields.short: Substitute address for emergency access.
fields.details: Only use if the address deliberately matches the service network. After repairing the main configuration, check whether the fallback is still needed.

fields.label: Fallback gateway
fields.short: Router address for fallback mode.
fields.details: For pure local maintenance access the gateway can stay empty or unused. For online updates/help it must be correct.

fields.label: Fallback subnet
fields.short: Netmask of the fallback address.
fields.details: Must match the fallback IP and the maintenance network.

fields.label: Fallback DNS
fields.short: Name server in fallback mode.
fields.details: Only relevant if the controller should resolve internet names in fallback mode.

fields.label: AP IP
fields.short: IP address of the controller access point.
fields.details: This address is used when a service device connects directly to the controller AP.

fields.label: AP SSID
fields.short: WLAN name of the local service access point.
fields.details: Should be unique so that several controllers on site are not confused.

fields.label: AP password
fields.short: Password for the service access point.
fields.details: An empty field keeps the stored password. WPA2 passwords need at least 8 characters; empty can be interpreted as an open service AP depending on the firmware.

fields.label: Select sequence
fields.short: Selects the scene/sequence slot being edited.
fields.details: Changes always refer to the currently selected sequence. Check the correct slot before copying or resetting.

fields.label: Time position in the sequence
fields.short: Shows a specific point in time of the sequence.
fields.details: Helps checking build-up, main phase and fade-out specifically.

fields.label: Preview speed
fields.short: Speed of the browser preview.
fields.details: Only affects the preview in the browser, not necessarily the real LED output.

fields.label: Global chase/wave synchronization
fields.short: Defines how several outputs run together in time.
fields.details: Start/stop synchronizes begin and end. Runtime uses the same step time per pixel, so short strings can finish earlier.

fields.label: Affected LEDs
fields.short: Determines whether fill values are interpreted as percent or absolute.
fields.details: Percent adapts to different output lengths. Absolute uses fixed LED counts and is limited per output.

fields.label: # pixels / fill level
fields.short: Determines how many LEDs are affected by the effect.
fields.details: Depending on the pixel mode, understood as a percentage or an absolute pixel count.

fields.label: Start/on/off effect
fields.short: Selects the effect for a sequence phase.
fields.details: Start is the build-up, on/main phase the permanent state, off the fade/tear-down phase.

fields.label: Start/main/off duration
fields.short: Duration or ramp of a sequence phase in milliseconds.
fields.details: Small values look hard and fast, larger values softer. Test the real output on very long LED strips.

fields.label: Start/on/off fill level
fields.short: Fill level of a phase.
fields.details: Controls how wide or full an effect appears within the phase.

fields.label: Step time ms
fields.short: Time between movement steps.
fields.details: Smaller values run faster. Too small values can look restless in long sequences.

fields.label: Pulse/blink period ms
fields.short: Period duration for pulse or blink effects.
fields.details: Determines how fast an effect gets brighter/darker or blinks.

fields.label: Transition duration ms
fields.short: Time for soft transitions.
fields.details: Larger values reduce hard jumps between states.

fields.label: Start/stop offset per channel
fields.short: Time offset between color or segment channels.
fields.details: Creates staggered movements. Very high values can make the effect hard to predict.

fields.label: Segment LEDs
fields.short: Block size in LEDs for segment lighting.
fields.details: Separate values for start, on and off allow changing segment widths within the sequence.

fields.label: Soft edge LEDs
fields.short: Number of LEDs for gentle fading at the segment edge.
fields.details: 0 is a hard edge. Larger values create softer transitions.

fields.label: Afterglow %
fields.short: Length of the tail or afterglow area.
fields.details: The bright head and the soft tail together make the visible length.

fields.label: Sparkle speed ms
fields.short: Speed for sparkle effects.
fields.details: Smaller values create more activity. Tune together with lifetime and fill level.

fields.label: Sparkle fill %
fields.short: Density of the sparkle pixels.
fields.details: High values look denser and brighter, but can strongly change current estimate and perception.

fields.label: Sparkle lifetime ms
fields.short: How long individual sparkle points stay visible.
fields.details: A short lifetime looks hectic, a long lifetime calmer.

fields.label: Tetris group min./max
fields.short: Size of the Tetris blocks.
fields.details: Min and max define the random range. Min should never be larger than max.

fields.label: Tetris gap
fields.short: Gap between Tetris blocks.
fields.details: Larger gaps make individual blocks clearer but reduce the visible fill.

fields.label: Tetris direction
fields.short: Direction or mirroring of the Tetris build-up.
fields.details: Reverse direction, mirror center and random direction can be set separately per phase.

fields.label: Tetris teardown
fields.short: Defines how built-up blocks disappear again.
fields.details: Depending on the mode reverse, random, wipe or soft teardown. Test in the preview and on real LEDs.

fields.label: Random fall time / pause
fields.short: Random ranges for Tetris timing.
fields.details: Min/max values create more organic movement. Extreme ranges can make the effect hard to plan.

fields.label: Tetris_2 next preview
fields.short: Shows the next block as a preview.
fields.details: Visual addition for Tetris_2. Increases the complexity of the effect.

fields.label: Tetris_2 synchronize segments
fields.short: Synchronizes Tetris_2 across segments.
fields.details: Useful with equal string segments or symmetric installations.

fields.label: Tetris_2 block size min./max
fields.short: Random range of the Tetris_2 block size.
fields.details: Smaller blocks look finer, larger blocks calmer and more massive.

fields.label: Tetris_2 speed min./max mm/s
fields.short: Physically based speed for Tetris_2.
fields.details: Together with pixels/meter this yields the visible movement speed.

fields.label: Tetris_2 pixels/meter
fields.short: LED density for the speed calculation.
fields.details: Must match the real installation if mm/s should look realistic.

fields.label: Tetris_2 early start
fields.short: Lets new blocks start before the previous one has fully finished.
fields.details: Chance and min/max define how often and how early overlapping starts happen.

fields.label: Tetris_2 HSV minimum distance
fields.short: Minimum distance between random colors.
fields.details: Higher values avoid very similar colors but can restrict the color selection.

fields.label: Status on/off TX
fields.short: KNX status object for the switching state.
fields.details: Sends the current on/off state to the KNX bus.

fields.label: Status scene TX
fields.short: KNX status object for the active scene.
fields.details: Helps visualizations display the current scene status.

fields.label: Status brightness TX
fields.short: KNX status object for brightness.
fields.details: Sends the current brightness value back.

fields.label: Status color R/G/B/W TX
fields.short: KNX status objects for color components.
fields.details: Reports the actually rendered output color: the arithmetic mean of the currently visible pixels per channel, including global and output brightness. During scenes, transitions and animations the value is a representative average and is sent rate-limited; an output that is off reports 0. A chain head averages across the whole chain. Only enable the channels you need.

fields.label: Status lock/force TX
fields.short: Feedback for lock and force state.
fields.details: Useful for visualization and diagnostics when operation is blocked or overridden.

fields.label: Status error code / power limit
fields.short: Feedback for errors and an active power limit.
fields.details: Allows KNX-side alarms or display of technical states.

fields.label: Admin code
fields.short: Opens the protected admin area.
fields.details: Admin is meant for diagnostics, JSON endpoints and deep technical information. Do not treat it as full network protection.

fields.label: Support snapshot
fields.short: Collects technical data for troubleshooting.
fields.details: For support questions, first load and copy the snapshot so that version, profile, pins, network, memory and recent events are visible.

fields.label: Factory defaults
fields.short: Resets the configuration to defaults.
fields.details: Only run deliberately and download a backup first. Afterwards re-check outputs, KNX and network.

fields.label: Passwords in export
fields.short: Controls whether sensitive data is contained in the backup.
fields.details: The standard export should not contain passwords in plain text. Use plain text only for deliberate local maintenance.

fields.label: Apply scene
fields.short: Starts a scene directly from the WebUI.
fields.details: Takes effect immediately on the active outputs. If KNX, lock, force or a manual test is active, the visible state can differ.

fields.label: Direct off
fields.short: Switches the LED output dark directly.
fields.details: Useful before updates, measurements or wiring work. KNX can set a new state again later.

fields.label: Brightness
fields.short: Direct brightness value for tests.
fields.details: Helps with quick checks without the sequence editor. Power limits and the output maximum brightness can still limit.

fields.label: R/G/B/W
fields.short: Direct color values for red, green, blue and white.
fields.details: Well suited for color order tests and quick visual checks. On RGB strips the white channel does not exist as a separate channel.

fields.label: Live load / standby / total
fields.short: Current estimate from the LED state.
fields.details: These values are computed, not measured. They help detect power limiter interventions and wrong pixel/color values.

fields.label: Safe limit
fields.short: Limit after the safety factor.
fields.details: Usable value computed from the controller or group limit and the safety percentage.

fields.label: Dim factor
fields.short: Shows whether the power limiter is currently dimming.
fields.details: 100 percent means no limiting. Lower values show active power reduction.

fields.label: All LEDs off mA
fields.short: Measured current with dark LEDs.
fields.details: This value is taken over as base current when the measurement profile is saved.

fields.label: Red/green/blue/white mA
fields.short: Measured values for individual color channels.
fields.details: After each test step, measure the current at the power supply and enter it. The firmware computes mA per pixel from this.

fields.label: RGB white mA
fields.short: Control measurement for red+green+blue together.
fields.details: Optional plausibility check. The value should roughly match the sum of the individual channels.

fields.label: Speed
fields.short: General effect speed.
fields.details: Depending on the effect, this value is used directly or together with step time, pixels/meter or phase duration.

fields.label: During ON / bounce
fields.short: Option for running or mirrored bouncing movement.
fields.details: Suitable for wave or chase effects that should not only start once.

fields.label: Fireworks speed / intensity
fields.short: Parameters for firework-like effects.
fields.details: Speed controls temporal activity, intensity the density or brightness impression.

fields.label: Tetrix speed / block width
fields.short: Parameters for the Tetrix effect.
fields.details: Block width determines the visible size, speed the movement.

fields.label: Version history
fields.short: List of installable or historical firmware versions.
fields.details: Allows updating to new versions or a deliberate rollback. Always save a backup before a rollback.

fields.label: Install this version
fields.short: Installs an entry from the version history.
fields.details: Only use firmware for the matching profile. The WebUI checks profile and file names; still create a backup first.

fields.label: Restart controller
fields.short: Restarts the controller via the WebUI.
fields.details: Useful after network or update changes. The WebUI is briefly unreachable.

fields.label: BOOTSEL / UF2 mode
fields.short: Puts the board into USB flash mode.
fields.details: Only use for maintenance via USB. The WebUI is unreachable afterwards until the board restarts or is flashed.

fields.label: Save configuration first
fields.short: Downloads a backup before firmware actions.
fields.details: Recommended before every update, rollback or local firmware upload.

fields.label: Event table
fields.short: Shows errors, warnings and runtime events.
fields.details: The newest entries help with diagnosis. For sporadic problems, save them as a support snapshot before clearing.

fields.label: LED backend
fields.short: Shows whether real LED output is active.
fields.details: If the backend is not ready or only virtual, configuration values are processed but not driven physically.

fields.label: LED profiles
fields.short: Number of different LED timing profiles.
fields.details: Many different profiles can make diagnosis and timing more complex. Configure identical strips identically where possible.

fields.label: Storage / LittleFS
fields.short: Status of the local file system.
fields.details: LittleFS stores configuration, locally loaded help and OTA helper data. On storage errors, save a backup and check the diagnostics.

fields.label: Release check
fields.short: Checks profile, update paths and release data.
fields.details: Helpful before releases so that manifest, version list, board profile and flash size fit together.

fields.label: Outputs / scene / estimated load
fields.short: Dashboard table for output status, scene and live load.
fields.details: Active outputs show real live load and scene. Disabled outputs are shown with status disabled, 0 mA, Output disabled and 0 active LEDs.

fields.label: Active outputs
fields.short: Counts active outputs relative to the provided configuration.
fields.details: The separate tiles Provided outputs and Board outputs were removed because the hardware maximum of the KLC board is 5 and the relevant operating value is the active outputs.

fields.label: Channel chaining (follows)
fields.short: Attaches this output as a follower of another channel; both act as one LED strip.
fields.details: The chain head (master) controls the whole chain: scene, KNX, maximum brightness and LED offset come from the head, effects run seamlessly across the total length. The follower inherits LED chip, LED colors and color order from the master and no longer reacts to KNX (no receive, no status). The follower keeps its own GPIO, pixel count, power group and string current limit. String segments are incompatible with chaining. Use the Walk chain test for alignment.

fields.label: Reverse in chain
fields.short: Reverses the pixel order of this chain link.
fields.details: Needed when a strip is physically installed against the chain direction. Telltale in the Walk chain test: the dot jumps to the end of the link at the seam and runs backwards. The chain head sets the direction and is never reversed.

fields.label: Walk chain
fields.short: Alignment aid: a dot runs once through the entire pixel space of the chain.
fields.details: Each link gets its own color and the start of each link stays dimly marked; one pass takes about 5 seconds. If the dot runs backwards at a seam, set Reverse in chain on that link. Stop: same button, Clear tests, or starting a scene.

fields.label: LAN failover
fields.short: If cable and WLAN share one subnet, only one interface serves the LAN; the other goes to standby.
fields.details: In a shared subnet replies could otherwise leave through the wrong interface (result: timeouts). The parked interface keeps its IP address but does not respond on it. If the active interface fails, the parked one takes over automatically within 1-2 seconds. Outbound priority selects the winner. In different subnets both interfaces stay reachable.

fields.label: Scene pool
fields.short: Adds this sequence to the pool cycled by the KNX object Scene next/previous.
fields.details: The pool contains all enabled sequences with the checkbox set, ascending by slot, wrapping at the end. KNX telegram 1 = next scene, 0 = previous. If the current scene is outside the pool or the channel is off, next jumps to the first and previous to the last pool entry.

fields.label: Scene next/previous
fields.short: 1-bit object: telegram 1 switches to the next, 0 to the previous scene from the scene pool.
fields.details: Exists per channel (default datapoints 105, 205, 305, 405, 505; group addresses from 2/2/26 in steps of 30) and centrally for all channels (datapoint 4, group address 2/2/4). The channel's current scene state is the pointer; there is no separate counter. The Scene pool checkbox in the sequence editor decides which sequences are in the pool.

fields.title: User and administrator
fields.body: There is exactly one user account and one administrator account. The user operates the lighting: starting and editing scenes and sequences, switching the view, changing language and appearance. The administrator may additionally change all system settings: network and Wi-Fi, firmware updates, configuration import and export, factory and network reset, KNX/BAOS base configuration, language package upload and the security settings themselves. All permissions are enforced on the server; direct URL or API calls follow the same rules as the navigation. Sign in on the /login page with role and password.

fields.title: Enabling/disabling user login
fields.body: User and administrator can enable or disable user login on the Security page. Enabled: the normal operating area requires a user or admin login. Disabled (factory state): operation is possible without signing in. The admin area always stays protected by the admin password in both cases. The interface language selection remains available without signing in and works completely offline.

fields.title: Simple and advanced view
fields.body: The simple view shows only the dashboard and the simplified sequence editor; the advanced view additionally shows all expert parameters. Switching views is purely a display mode and not a security role: even in the advanced view, admin functions stay locked until an admin login. User and administrator can switch the view at any time on the system page; this never grants admin rights.

fields.title: Default passwords
fields.body: From the factory and after a factory reset the following apply: user password 123456, admin password Admin (case-sensitive). User login is initially disabled; admin protection is always active. As long as default passwords are active, the interface shows a clear security warning. Please change both passwords on the Security page after commissioning.

fields.title: Changing passwords
fields.body: Passwords are changed on the Security page. The new password is entered twice (maximum 64 characters, not empty). Changing the admin password additionally requires the current admin password and signs out all admin sessions afterwards. The administrator can set a new user password without the previous one (clearly marked as an admin action); a signed-in user changes their own password by confirming the current one. Passwords are stored only as salt plus PBKDF2 hash, never in plain text, and never appear in configuration exports or logs.

fields.title: Forgotten admin password (recovery)
fields.body: There is no master password and no hidden unlock path. If the admin password is lost, only the service button on the device helps: holding it for 2 to just under 5 seconds resets only the network settings; holding it for 5 to just under 10 seconds performs a full factory reset. After the factory reset the default credentials apply again (user 123456, admin Admin, user login disabled) and the service AP is reachable.

fields.title: Protected beta update flow
fields.body: Calling /update/beta-latest via GET no longer starts an installation: after an admin login it only shows a check and confirmation page with the available beta version. The actual installation happens exclusively via an explicit POST with a valid admin session, CSRF token and confirmation. Browser preview, link scanners or reloading the page can no longer trigger an installation.

fields.title: Uploading a language package offline
fields.body: On the system page the administrator can upload a language package (JSON, maximum 256 KB) directly from a PC or smartphone - even completely without internet, for example in the service AP. The file is fully validated (UTF-8, JSON syntax, key set, language code, firmware range, size) and only activated atomically after a successful check; on any error the previous language stays active. The file name does not matter, the selected target language is decisive. The built-in English always remains available as fallback and cannot be deleted.

fields.label: Pending configuration
fields.short: Active means a configuration that completed the entire startup path. Test values on /outputs are volatile RAM values, reuse the fixed test pool and are never saved automatically. Saved structural changes are pending and become active only after a reboot. Pending becomes Last Known Good only after the master pool, ranges, PIO, DMA, every required output and the 64 KiB system reserve have succeeded. A failure is rolled back completely and Last Known Good is started; if that also fails, LEDs remain off in safe recovery mode while WebUI and service AP stay reachable. The LED budget is 128 KiB including the test pool. Zero pixels are allowed only for a volatile no-output test; one pixel safely uses pixel 0 for both ends; up to 800 is normal, 801 to 1200 is the warning range, and 1201 is rejected. A chained output is protected as a complete chain and a follower is never tested alone.
